title: Kitchen Renovation Near Me Cost: Local UK Guide
description: Kitchen renovation near me cost explained: local UK price ranges, quote factors and practical tips for comparing like-for-like estimates.

blocks.text: Searching for “kitchen renovation near me cost” usually means you want more than a national average. You need to know what a kitchen project could cost in your area, what is included in the estimate and whether two local companies are pricing the same work. In Watford, Hertfordshire, North London and Bedfordshire, a kitchen renovation can range from a straightforward replacement of units and worktops to a complete redesign involving plumbing, electrics, flooring, tiling and structural work. As a rough guide, a professionally fitted kitchen renovation may typically cost between £10,000 and £35,000, while smaller refreshes may cost less and high-specification or structurally altered kitchens may cost considerably more. Every project and specification differs, so use these figures only for early planning and request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
What does a local kitchen renovation typically cost?

The most useful way to think about cost is by project scope. A cosmetic update, such as repainting, replacing handles, changing a worktop or installing new flooring, may typically cost roughly £3,000 to £10,000, depending on the materials and amount of labour. This is not usually a full renovation, but it can improve a tired kitchen without moving services or replacing every cabinet. As a rough guide, a standard replacement kitchen, including new units, worktops, appliances, fitting and associated finishing work, may typically fall around £12,000 to £25,000. A larger renovation with upgraded cabinets, bespoke storage, more expensive appliances, new lighting, floor and wall finishes, or changes to plumbing may typically cost around £25,000 to £45,000 or more. If walls are removed, openings are altered or the kitchen forms part of a wider house renovation, the building work can make the total substantially higher. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Which parts of the quote affect the price?

Cabinet choice is often one of the largest variables. Flat-pack, rigid, made-to-measure and bespoke cabinets can have different manufacturing and installation costs. The internal layout matters too: a run of standard base units is usually more straightforward than a kitchen with tall housings, islands, curved units, integrated appliances, pull-out storage or difficult access. Worktops range from laminate to timber, composite and natural stone, with fabrication, templating and installation affecting the final figure.

Keeping the sink, dishwasher, cooker and radiators in their existing positions can help control costs. Moving water, waste, gas or electrical points adds labour and may require additional materials or coordination. Lighting upgrades, extra sockets, ventilation, underfloor heating and changes to electrical arrangements can also change the electrical element of the quote. Do not assume that decorating, plaster repairs, splashbacks, tiling, flooring, waste removal or final cleaning are included: some companies include these items and others list them separately. Access is another practical consideration. A terraced property, flat, narrow stairway or limited parking may take longer to move materials into and waste out of the building.

blocks.text: How to compare kitchen renovation quotes like for like

A low headline price is not necessarily better value if important work has been left out. Before comparing estimates, give each renovation company the same brief: plans or measurements where available, appliance preferences, desired finishes, whether walls or services are moving, and the level of preparation required. Ask for a written, itemised quotation rather than relying on a single total. BMB Renovation offers kitchen fitting and renovation and free, no-obligation quotes. You can also review [kitchen fitting in Watford](/kitchen-fitting-watford) if Watford is your project location.
Questions to ask before accepting an estimate

items: Does the price include VAT, delivery, installation and removal of the old kitchen?
Are cabinets, handles, worktops, sinks, taps and appliances listed by model or specification?
Which plumbing, electrical, tiling, plastering, flooring and decorating tasks are included?
Who supplies materials, and what happens if an item arrives damaged or is delayed?
How are unexpected problems, such as damaged subfloors or concealed pipework, priced and approved?
Is the estimate based on a site visit, and are access, parking and waste removal included?
What payment stages, expected programme and practical handover arrangements are proposed?

blocks.text: Choosing a reputable local renovation company

Look for clarity rather than an impressive-sounding promise. A reputable contractor should be willing to explain the specification, identify exclusions and distinguish confirmed costs from provisional allowances. Check that the business can cover the trades your project needs, and ask how responsibility is managed when several types of work are involved. Before appointing any company, discuss your exact address, scope and finish level rather than assuming that a price from another property will transfer directly to yours.

It is sensible to obtain several detailed estimates, but avoid choosing solely on the lowest figure. Compare the quality and durability of the proposed materials, how much preparation is allowed for, whether the same person will coordinate the work and how variations are recorded. If one quote is much cheaper, ask what has been omitted. Conversely, a higher quote may reflect better cabinets, more comprehensive preparation or a fuller range of finishing trades. Ways to keep a kitchen renovation within budget

Start with the layout. Keeping the existing plumbing and electrical positions is often less expensive than moving them, although the condition and suitability of the current services still need checking. Spend more on items that are difficult to replace later, such as cabinets, worktops and durable flooring, while choosing carefully where a mid-range product will perform just as well. Confirm appliance dimensions before final cabinet orders, allow for filler panels and end panels, and keep a contingency for unforeseen work in an older property. Most importantly, finalise the scope before work starts and record any changes in writing, including the revised price and effect on timing. This makes the final cost easier to manage and gives you a fair basis for comparing local kitchen renovation estimates.

faq.q: What is usually included in a kitchen renovation quote?
faq.a: It may include cabinets, worktops, fitting and some services, but plumbing, electrics, appliances, tiling, flooring, waste removal, VAT and decorating can vary. Check every item and exclusion in writing.

faq.q: How many kitchen renovation quotes should I get?
faq.a: Getting two or three detailed quotes can be a practical comparison. Give each company the same brief and compare the specification, exclusions, allowances, programme and payment terms rather than just the total.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to keep the existing kitchen layout?
faq.a: Often, yes. Retaining the positions of plumbing, waste, gas and electrical points can reduce labour and materials, although the existing services still need to be assessed for condition and suitability.

faq.q: Can a local renovation company handle all the kitchen trades?
faq.a: Some companies coordinate or handle several trades, while others use separate subcontractors. Ask who is responsible for plumbing, electrics, tiling, cabinet installation and finishing work before accepting a quote.
